data.description: Learn what's behind The Mule. Mule Box is dedicated to always being our customer's preferred portable self-storage container provider for all their moving and storage needs.

data.title: About Us
data.description: Mule Box is an independently-owned and operated mobile storage company. We deliver weather-resistant, 16-foot and 20-foot (where available) portable storage containers to homes and businesses when they are moving, renovating or needing to secure their supplies and equipment onsite. For those moving, we transport the filled container to their desired location or can store it at one of our local and secure facilities.

data.title: Our Promise
data.description: Mule Box will work tirelessly to provide the perfect fit for your onsite and temporary storage needs.

data.title: Our Story – Two Men and a Mule
data.description:
Our founders, Steve and Jack, have both spent their careers making good brands even better. Steve as a former founder and owner of an advertising agency that helped grow national, regional and local brands. Jack as a high-level marketing executive of retail and restaurants brands (and also as a leading franchisee in a national window replacement franchise).

In that spirit, they recognized an opportunity to create a portable self-storage brand that stands out from the competition. A brand that is fun, locally-owned in each market by a franchisee and a brand that customers could better relate to (who doesn't love a mule?). A brand that doesn't offer a call center, but instead offers real, live local people in the markets they serve. And, most importantly, a brand who sole focus is delivering 5-star service with every portable self-storage rental experience.

The result: Mule Box, a brand stubbornly devoted to bringing portable storage and moving solutions to local neighbors. Every day the Mule Box brand gains more fans as Mule Box kicks some much-needed life and personality into the portable storage industry.

members.name: Steve Choppin
members.bio: Steve’s background is in advertising and marketing. During his time working for some of America's top advertising agencies, he helped launch several national and regional brands, developed strong lead generation strategies and results for marketers and was a part of building brands for several industry stalwarts (Metro by T-Mobile, Motel 6, KFC and Taco Cabana to name a few). This gave Steve an appreciation for the power of strong customer relationships, which is something his Mule Box customers appreciate as well.

members.name: Jack Civa
members.bio: Jack enjoyed a long, distinguished career in marketing leadership roles within franchised retail and restaurant chains. Jack worked on leading national and regional brands such a Fogo de Chao, Taco Cabana, Jamba Juice and many others. Jack's passion for franchising inspired him to leave the corporate world and run his own Window World franchises (he now owns two). And today, Jack’s well-honed skills are helping to build the Mule Box brand as it seeks to transform the portable self-storage industry one new Mule Box location at a time.

items.question: Does Mule Box serve my area?
items.answer: Mule Box is growing fast and is always on the move. [Click here](/locations) to see if we're in your market.

items.question: How much can I fit in a Mule Box?
items.answer: We offer 16′ X 8′ X 8′ boxes and in some select markets 20'x8'x8' boxes. Use our chart to help decide how many Mule Box containers you need.

items.question: Do you offer moving services?
items.answer: While we do not move or pack your belongings for you, our local markets can provide a list of customer-recommended hourly moving companies that serve your area to make your move as easy as possible. Please contact your respective location to find out more.

items.question: How do I schedule a Mule Box container delivery?
items.answer: Fill out our online Instant Quote form. It’s that easy.

items.question: When will my Mule Box portable container arrive?
items.answer: We will notify you by email and/or text. Remember, you do not have to be present for delivery.

items.question: What can I load in my Mule Box portable moving container?
items.answer: Almost anything can be placed in your Mule Box. However, there are some exceptions. Hazardous materials (toxic chemicals, gas, liquids, waste, lawn mowers, motorized vehicles, etc.) and animals are strictly prohibited. In addition, we recommend that heirlooms, legal documents and currency not be placed in your Mule Box.

items.question: How long do I have to load and unload my Mule Box?
items.answer: Because we offer monthly rental, you can pack and unload at your own pace. Your billing cycle begins the day your Mule Box is delivered and continues through your rental anniversary date.

items.question: How long can I keep my Mule Box portable storage unit at my location?
items.answer: Unless there is a restriction in your neighborhood, you can keep it as long as you need it. We will bill you appropriately for the additional use.

items.question: Can I have more than one Mule Box at my home?
items.answer: Yes, if your driveway can fit two vehicles side by side or end to end, it can likely accommodate two Mule Boxes. There is no limit on the # of boxes you can rent from The Mule.

items.question: Do my items in the Mule Box need to be packed?
items.answer: To help prevent damage, we recommend that all your items be wrapped, padded or placed in a box. Our boxes also have d-rings every 2 feet high and low that you can use ratchet straps on for additional security.

items.question: Does Mule Box sell moving supplies?
items.answer: While we do not sell or rent cardboard boxes or moving blankets-- we do sell disc locks to help secure your contents.

items.question: When can I access my Mule Box while it’s stored at your facility?
items.answer: Access at our facilities is by appointment only. Contact your local market to schedule a time and inquire if additional costs apply.

items.question: Do I need insurance?
items.answer: Mule Box provides a sure-footed moving and storage process, taking great care to protect your belongings. But weather, road conditions and other events can be out of our control. The Mule Box Rental Agreement offers customers the option to have coverage for the containers and their contents.

items.question: Is the container insured?
items.answer: Our optional Mule Box Container Damage Waiver covers accidental loss or damage to the container. The optional Storage Protectors Contents Insurance policies will save you the hassle of filing on your homeowner’s insurance policy and come with a significantly LOWER deductible.

items.question: Do you provide insurance for my belongings?
items.answer: Mule Box offers optional Storage Protectors Content Insurance coverage. It has a low-deductible, and we offer policies covering all types of levels of insurance to make sure your goods are covered.

items.question: Do actual mules deliver your storage containers?
items.answer: No, although their exceptional endurance and strength mean that they probably could. Our Mule Boxes are delivered by trucks, while our Mule-Bot™ delivery system loads and unloads the units. This wireless system can deliver storage containers in tight spaces and keeps them level to reduce shifting of contents during the load and unloading process.

items.question: Why are you called Mule Box?
items.answer: Because we have a lot of the same characteristics of a mule. We are loyal, intelligent, hardworking, determined and sure-footed. With these qualities who wouldn't love having a Mule on their side?

entries.body_markdown:
Moving to a new home can be exciting, but moving within the Bay Area comes with its own unique challenges. From navigating busy streets and steep hills to coordinating parking, apartment access, narrow driveways, and different neighborhoods, a local Bay Area move requires planning and preparation.

Whether you're relocating from the East Bay to the Peninsula, moving from the Peninsula to the South Bay, or simply changing neighborhoods, choosing the right moving and storage option can make the entire process easier.

For many Bay Area residents, renting a portable storage box can be a convenient and cost-effective alternative to hiring a traditional moving company. Instead of rushing to load a moving truck on a specific day, a portable storage container gives you the flexibility to pack and load your belongings at your own pace. Once you're ready, your portable storage box can be transported from your current home to your new home, as long as both locations are within the Bay Area.

Mule Box is a locally owned and operated portable storage company serving Fremont, Milpitas, San Jose, Santa Clara, Sunnyvale, Mountain View, Campbell, Palo Alto, East Palo Alto, Menlo Park, Atherton, Cupertino, Los Altos, Los Gatos, Saratoga, Newark, Hayward, Castro Valley, Union City, Pleasanton, Livermore, Dublin, and San Ramon. We provide portable storage boxes that make moving, relocating, decluttering, renovating, and storing your belongings easier and more flexible.

With October approaching, now is a great time to start planning your Bay Area move. Here's what you should know.

## Why Portable Storage Can Be a Great Option for a Bay Area Move

When people think about moving, they often think about hiring a moving company, renting a moving truck, or asking friends and family to help.

But there is another option: portable storage.

With a portable storage box, the container is delivered directly to you. You can load your belongings yourself, on your own schedule, without having to rush everything into a truck in a single day.

entries.body_markdown:
You’ve got a portable storage container sitting in your driveway, a house full of belongings, and one big question: How are you going to fit everything inside without turning it into a giant game of Tetris?

The good news is that you probably have more storage space than you think.

With the right packing strategy, our 16-foot × 8-foot × 8-foot portable storage containers can hold the contents of approximately 2–3 rooms, depending on the size and type of belongings being stored.

Whether you’re moving to a new home, remodeling, decluttering, staging your house, or simply need extra storage space on your property, packing your portable storage container correctly can help you maximize every available inch while keeping your belongings protected.

At Mule Box, we’re a family-owned and operated portable storage business serving Fremont, Milpitas, San Jose, Santa Clara, Sunnyvale, Mountain View, Campbell, Palo Alto, East Palo Alto, Menlo Park, Atherton, Cupertino, Los Altos, Los Gatos, Saratoga, Newark, Hayward, Castro Valley, Union City, Pleasanton, Livermore, Dublin, and San Ramon.We provide modern portable storage containers designed to make moving and storage more convenient, secure, and efficient.

Here are our best tips for getting the most out of your portable storage container.

## 1. Organize Your Belongings Before Loading

One of the biggest mistakes people make is starting to load a portable storage container without a plan. Before anything goes inside, organize your belongings by size, weight, and how frequently you’ll need access to them.

### Use sturdy, similarly sized boxes

Standard-size moving boxes are easier to stack than a collection of boxes in completely different shapes and sizes. Strong boxes also help prevent your belongings from shifting or collapsing during storage.

Clearly label each box with:

- Its contents
- The room it belongs to
- Whether it contains fragile items
- Whether you’ll need easy access to it

If you know you’ll need certain items before everything else, mark those boxes accordingly and place them where they’ll be easiest to reach.

### Don’t leave empty space inside boxes

Fill empty areas inside boxes with towels, blankets, clothing, or packing paper. This helps prevent items from shifting while also providing additional protection. Just be careful not to overpack boxes to the point that they become too heavy or difficult to safely lift.

### Create a simple inventory

For larger moves or long-term storage, consider creating a basic inventory of what you’re storing. You can also take photos of valuable or important belongings before they go into the container. A little organization at the beginning can save you a lot of time later.

## 2. Properly Wrap Furniture and Appliances

Furniture and appliances are some of the largest and most expensive items you’re likely to put into a portable storage container, so give them some extra protection.

### Protect furniture surfaces

Wrap sofas, chairs, mattresses, tables, dressers, and other furniture with moving blankets, furniture pads, or other appropriate protective materials. For upholstered furniture, use breathable furniture covers when appropriate. Avoid trapping moisture against furniture for extended periods. For wood furniture, protect corners and surfaces from scratches and impacts. When practical, remove drawers and secure them separately so they don’t slide open during handling.

### Protect appliances

Clean and completely dry appliances before storing them. For refrigerators and freezers, make sure they are fully dry before storage and leave the doors positioned according to the manufacturer’s storage recommendations. Use padding around appliances to help prevent scratches and contact with other items.

### Disassemble large furniture when practical

If a table, bed frame, shelving unit, or other large item can safely be disassembled, doing so can significantly improve your use of space. Keep screws, bolts, brackets, and other hardware together in labeled bags. Store or attach the hardware with the corresponding furniture so it’s easy to find when you’re ready to reassemble everything. The goal isn’t simply to fill the container. The goal is to use the space efficiently while protecting your belongings.

## 3. Stack From Floor to Ceiling

This is one of the most important tips for maximizing portable storage container space: Think vertically. Our containers are approximately 8 feet high, so don’t only think about how much floor space you have. Think about how much usable space you have from the floor all the way to the ceiling. Start with your heaviest and sturdiest belongings on the bottom, then work your way upward.

### Put heavy items on the bottom

Place heavier boxes, sturdy furniture, and other substantial items toward the bottom of your load. Place lighter boxes and less durable belongings toward the top. This helps protect fragile items and creates a more stable load.

### Build stable walls

Whenever possible, stack boxes and belongings tightly together without forcing them into place. Think of your load as building a stable wall from one side of the container to the other. Avoid creating tall stacks of loose or unstable items that could fall when the doors are opened.

### Fill the gaps

Once your larger items are positioned, look for smaller spaces. That space between a dresser and a box? Use it. The area underneath a table? Use it. The space inside certain furniture pieces? It may be usable too, depending on the item. Small belongings can often fit inside larger pieces of furniture, helping you make the most of your available storage space. Just be careful not to place heavy objects inside furniture that isn’t designed to support the additional weight.

### Keep important items accessible

If you know you’ll need access to certain belongings, don’t bury them behind everything else. Place frequently needed items closer to the doors or create a small access area when possible.

## 4. Balance the Weight if Your Container Is Being Transported

If your portable storage container will be transported to another location, proper weight distribution becomes especially important. Distribute weight as evenly as possible throughout the container rather than concentrating most of the heavy items in one area.

A good rule of thumb is:

- Keep heavier belongings low.
- Place lighter belongings higher.
- Distribute weight throughout the container.
- Avoid creating an excessively heavy area on one side.

This creates a more stable load and helps keep the weight distributed appropriately during transportation.

### Secure belongings for transport

Items can shift while a container is being transported, even when everything initially looks perfectly organized. Use appropriate ratchet straps and tie-downs to secure furniture and other items when relocating the container. Secure taller or potentially unstable items so they don’t shift or fall into other belongings.

**Important:** Use tie-down equipment correctly and only attach straps to appropriate structural points. Never rely on a fragile piece of furniture, shelving, or another unsecured item as an anchor point.

If your container is staying on your property, extensive transport-related weight balancing and tie-down requirements may not apply in the same way. However, stable stacking and safe packing are still important.

## 5. Never Store Hazardous or Prohibited Items

Portable storage containers are designed for household and business storage—not hazardous materials. Never place hazardous, illegal, or prohibited items inside a portable storage container.

Examples may include:

- Fuel or gasoline
- Propane or other compressed gas cylinders
- Paint, solvents, and certain chemicals
- Explosives or fireworks
- Toxic or hazardous substances
- Illegal items
- Perishable food
- Items that are wet or likely to leak
- Other materials prohibited by your storage provider or applicable laws

Motorized vehicles and other unusually heavy or specialized items may also be prohibited or require specific arrangements.

**When in doubt, call Mule Box before loading the item.**

It’s always better to ask first than discover later that something cannot be transported or stored.

## 6. Prepare Your Loading Area Before Delivery

Our delivery system is designed to maneuver into surprisingly tight spaces, but giving our delivery equipment as much room as possible makes the process easier. Before your scheduled delivery, clear the area around the planned loading location.

Remove:

- Parked vehicles
- Lawn furniture
- Toys
- Trash cans
- Garden equipment
- Low-hanging branches
- Other obstacles

Also make sure the area is accessible to our delivery equipment. A clear loading zone helps create a smoother and more efficient portable storage container delivery, loading, and unloading process.

## Why the Portable Storage Container You Choose Matters

Not all portable storage containers are built the same. When you’re trusting a company with your household belongings, the construction and features of the container matter. At Mule Box Bay Area, we believe our customers deserve modern, durable storage equipment and not an aging box that has been circulating from customer to customer for years. Our portable storage containers are made with 100% steel construction and are designed with features that provide a strong, secure environment for your belongings.

### 100% Steel Construction

Our containers are built with 100% steel rather than plywood construction, providing a durable structure designed for repeated use and transportation.

### Ventilated for Better Air Circulation

Our containers are ventilated to promote air circulation and help with temperature management inside the storage space.

Our portable storage containers are designed to protect your belongings from outdoor weather conditions, making them a practical option for storing items on your property.

### Secure Swing-Open Doors

Our containers feature secure swing-open doors that provide a wide opening for loading and unloading furniture, appliances, boxes, and other belongings. Unlike some storage containers that use roll-up doors, our swing-open door design provides a substantial, solid entry point and secure locking system.

### Modern Equipment From a Local Family-Owned Business

At Mule Box, we’re proud to offer newer, modern portable storage containers while providing the personal service you’d expect from a family-owned and operated local business. We don’t believe you should have to choose between convenient portable storage and quality equipment.

## How Much Can a 16-Foot Portable Storage Container Hold?

Our 16' × 8' × 8' portable storage containers provide approximately 1,024 cubic feet of storage space. When packed efficiently, that can accommodate the belongings from approximately 2–3 rooms, depending on the size of the rooms and the amount and type of furniture and household goods. Actual capacity will vary significantly from household to household. A home with large sectional sofas, oversized furniture, exercise equipment, and other bulky belongings will use space differently than a home primarily filled with boxes and smaller furniture. That’s why efficient packing matters so much.

### Portable Storage Packing Checklist

Before you start loading your container, keep this checklist handy:

- Sort and organize belongings before loading
- Use sturdy, appropriately sized moving boxes
- Label boxes clearly
- Wrap furniture with moving blankets or appropriate protective materials
- Protect appliances and fragile belongings
- Disassemble large furniture when practical
- Place heavy items on the bottom
- Stack upward to maximize the 8-foot interior height
- Place lighter items on top
- Fill appropriate gaps without creating unstable stacks
- Keep frequently needed items accessible
- Use proper ratchet straps/tie-downs when relocating
- Distribute weight evenly when the container will be transported
- Never store hazardous or prohibited materials
- Keep the delivery/loading area clear
- Confirm questionable items with us before loading

### Make Your Portable Storage Space Work Harder for You

Packing a portable storage container doesn’t have to be overwhelming. With a little planning, proper protection, and smart stacking, you can make a significant difference in how much you can fit inside your container and how easy it will be to find your belongings later.

entries.title: El Niño Storm Preparedness: How Bay Area Homeowners Can Prepare Their Homes, Families, and Belongings

frontmatter.description: With El Niño strengthening for the 2026–27 winter season, now is a good time for Bay Area homeowners to take a closer look at their homes and emergency preparedness plans.

entries.body_markdown:
When the first major winter storm arrives in the Bay Area, it is usually too late to start thinking about the things that could have been done weeks or even months earlier. A clogged gutter, a leaking roof, an unsecured backyard structure, a dead generator battery, or important belongings stored in a low-lying garage can quickly turn a heavy rainstorm into a much bigger headache.

With El Niño strengthening for the 2026–27 winter season, now is a good time for Bay Area homeowners to take a closer look at their homes and emergency preparedness plans. NOAA currently reports a greater than 90% chance of a very strong El Niño during the Northern Hemisphere fall and winter, and current forecasts give a significant possibility of an event ranking among the strongest in the historical record. That does not mean every Bay Area community will experience severe weather, but it is a good reminder that preparing before a storm is almost always easier than dealing with damage afterward.

For homeowners throughout the San Francisco Bay Area, storm preparedness isn't about expecting the worst. It is about being ready for the possibilities.

## What Does El Niño Mean for Bay Area Homeowners?

El Niño is a naturally occurring climate pattern involving warmer-than-average ocean temperatures in the tropical Pacific. Its effects can influence weather patterns across the United States, including California.

A strong El Niño can increase the odds of certain weather patterns, but it does not guarantee a particular amount of rain, flooding, wind, or storm damage in every location. That makes preparation especially important: instead of trying to predict exactly what will happen, homeowners can focus on the things they can control.

For Bay Area residents, that means looking at potential problems such as:

- Heavy rain and localized flooding
- Roof and gutter problems
- Water intrusion around doors and windows
- Storm-drain backups
- Fallen trees and branches
- Power outages
- Wind damage
- Mud, debris, and drainage issues
- Water damage to belongings stored in garages, sheds, and lower levels
- Temporary difficulty accessing roads or leaving home
- Damage caused by items left unsecured outdoors

A few hours of preparation can make a meaningful difference when bad weather arrives.

## Start With the Outside of Your Home

One of the easiest ways to prepare for a major storm is to walk around your property before the rain starts. Look for anything that could become a problem once strong winds and heavy rainfall arrive.

### Clean Gutters and Downspouts

Leaves, dirt, and debris can prevent water from flowing away from your roof and foundation properly. Clean gutters and make sure downspouts direct water away from your home's foundation. If you have extensions that are damaged, disconnected, or missing, replace them before the rainy season gets underway.

### Check Your Roof

You don't necessarily need to replace an entire roof to prepare for winter storms. Sometimes small maintenance issues can become expensive problems when heavy rain arrives. Look for missing or damaged shingles, cracked flashing, damaged vents, and areas where water may already be getting inside. If you notice signs of a leak, have the problem evaluated before the next major storm.

### Trim Problematic Trees and Branches

Trees are beautiful and an important part of many Bay Area neighborhoods, but large branches hanging over roofs, driveways, fences, or power lines deserve attention. Have questionable trees or branches inspected by a qualified professional, particularly if they appear dead, damaged, diseased, or unstable.

### Secure Outdoor Items

Patio furniture, umbrellas, garbage cans, decorations, tools, lightweight structures, and other outdoor items can become damaged or cause damage during high winds. Before a major storm, secure or move anything that could blow around your property.

### Don't Forget the Areas You Rarely Think About

Storm preparation isn't only about the roof. Some of the most frustrating water damage can happen in areas homeowners don't routinely inspect.

Check:

- Garage doors and weather stripping
- Basement or lower-level areas
- Crawl spaces
- Window and skylight seals
- Exterior doors
- Foundation drainage
- Sump pumps, if applicable
- Retaining walls
- Driveways and drainage channels
- Outdoor drains
- Fences and gates

Pay particular attention to areas where water has accumulated during previous storms. Past problems are often clues about where future problems may develop.

## Protect the Belongings You Don't Want to Lose

One of the most overlooked parts of storm preparedness is protecting the things inside your home.

Many families keep holiday decorations, furniture, photographs, business equipment, tools, appliances, important documents, and other valuable possessions in garages, sheds, closets, and storage areas. If those areas experience water intrusion, the belongings can become damaged before you even realize there is a problem. This is where getting belongings off the floor can make a surprisingly big difference.

Use shelving, pallets, waterproof containers, and elevated storage whenever practical. Important documents and irreplaceable items should receive additional protection and, when possible, should be stored somewhere less vulnerable to water damage.

## A Portable Storage Container Can Be More Than Just Storage

A portable storage box or portable storage container is often associated with moving, remodeling, decluttering, or creating extra storage space. But homeowners sometimes overlook how useful portable storage can be when preparing for an emergency. Mule Box can give homeowners another place to temporarily store belongings while they prepare their property for severe weather.

For example, if you are:

- Remodeling a room before winter
- Replacing windows or doors
- Repairing a roof
- Waterproofing part of your home
- Cleaning out a garage
- Moving valuable furniture away from an area vulnerable to water intrusion
- Protecting belongings while construction or repairs are underway
- Temporarily relocating possessions after storm damage
- Making room for emergency repairs

Having a secure storage space available on your property can make the process considerably easier.

There is another benefit people don't always consider: a portable storage container can give you flexibility when the unexpected happens. If part of your home needs repairs after a storm, you may suddenly need somewhere to put furniture, boxes, appliances, tools, or other belongings while contractors work. Having portable storage already available can help keep those items organized and out of the way while you deal with the repair itself. That is one reason portable storage can be useful far beyond moving day.

## Build a Bay Area Emergency Supply Kit

Storm preparation should also include supplies that allow your household to function if the electricity goes out or you cannot easily leave home.

California's Office of Emergency Services recommends keeping flashlights available throughout the home, charging phones and power banks, and planning for necessities such as water, nonperishable food, and blankets during power outages.

Consider keeping the following supplies somewhere easy for your family to access:

- Flashlights
- Extra batteries
- Battery-powered or hand-crank radio
- Portable phone chargers and power banks
- Backup charging cables
- First-aid supplies
- Bottled water
- Nonperishable food
- Manual can opener
- Blankets and warm clothing
- Basic tools
- Emergency contact information
- Copies of important documents
- Pet food and pet supplies
- Necessary medications
- Battery-powered lights
- Work gloves
- Waterproof storage bags or containers
- Fire extinguisher
- Cash in small denominations

A generator can also be useful during a prolonged power outage, but it is important to operate generators safely. Never run a fuel-burning generator inside a house, garage, or other enclosed space because of the risk of deadly carbon monoxide buildup. Follow the manufacturer's instructions and applicable safety guidance.

## Think About the Power Going Out Before It Happens

A power outage can be more than an inconvenience. Refrigerators and freezers can lose power. Garage doors may not operate normally. Internet service may be interrupted. Phones eventually run out of battery. Some households may depend on electrically powered equipment.

Before storm season, identify everything in your home that depends on electricity and make a backup plan where possible. Charge portable batteries before severe weather arrives and make sure everyone in the household knows where flashlights and emergency supplies are stored. It sounds simple, but during a nighttime power outage, knowing exactly where the flashlight is can suddenly become very important.

## Protect Your Home From Water Before You See Water

One of the best storm preparation strategies is to deal with small problems before they become large ones.

If you have noticed:

- A ceiling stain
- A recurring roof leak
- Water around a window
- Dampness in a garage
- Standing water near your foundation
- A slow-draining area
- A damaged gutter
- Cracked exterior caulking

Don't wait for the biggest storm of the season to find out whether it gets worse. Schedule repairs while contractors and materials are readily available.

The same principle applies to home improvements. Improving drainage, repairing weather seals, maintaining the roof, improving exterior drainage, replacing damaged gutters, installing appropriate sump-pump systems where applicable, and addressing vulnerable areas around the home can all be worthwhile investments in protecting your property.

## Small Preparations Can Prevent Big Problems

Storm preparedness doesn't have to mean spending thousands of dollars or turning your house into a fortress. Sometimes the most valuable preparation involves simple things like cleaning the gutters, moving boxes off the garage floor, charging the power banks, checking the roof, securing patio furniture, trimming a problematic branch, finding the flashlight, taking pictures of your belongings for insurance records, knowing where the water shutoff is located, or having a plan for pets.

These aren't dramatic preparations. They're practical ones. And practical preparation is exactly what homeowners should be thinking about before severe weather arrives.

## Why a Local, Family-Owned Storage Company Can Make a Difference

At Mule Box, we're a small, family-owned and operated portable storage business serving the Bay Area. Being local and family operated matters, particularly when weather or other unexpected events create a sudden need for storage.

Large disasters can create a lot of moving parts at once. Homeowners may need temporary storage while repairs are being completed, contractors may need additional space for a project, and families may need somewhere secure to keep belongings while they figure out their next steps.

As a local Bay Area business, our goal isn't simply to drop off a storage container and disappear. We understand that our customers are storing their homes, possessions, memories, tools, furniture, and sometimes the things that matter most to them.

Portable storage can be useful before, during, and after an emergency and you don't have to wait until something goes wrong to take advantage of it.

## Prepare Now, Worry Less Later

Nobody can predict exactly what the 2026–27 winter will bring to the Bay Area. Even a very strong El Niño does not guarantee that every community will experience major flooding, damaging winds, or severe storms. What we can do is prepare for the possibilities.

Take a walk around your home. Look at the roof. Clean the gutters. Check the drainage. Secure the backyard. Put together an emergency kit. Charge your backup batteries. Think about where your belongings would go if part of your home needed repairs.

And if you need additional space to protect and organize your belongings before, during, or after a storm, consider whether a portable storage container makes sense for your situation. The best time to prepare for a storm is when the sky is still clear, the driveway is still dry, and you have time to think.

If you are a Bay Area homeowner looking for portable storage containers, portable storage boxes, temporary storage, or on-site storage, give Mule Box a call. Prepare for the possibilities. Protect what matters. And give yourself one less thing to worry about when the rain finally comes.
